\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.SpaceAmplifyPolyCode}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Machine code bound]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.codeBound}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.codeBound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.codeK, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and natural numbers $n,S$, define its
code bound to be $2^{\operatorname{codeK}(N)(S+\operatorname{logSpace}(n)+1)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepting configuration]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
A configuration is accepting if its machine state is absent, indicating that the machine
has halted, and its output tape contains exactly the one-symbol string consisting of
true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance probability]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.randProb, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
For a configuration $C$ of a finite nondeterministic Turing machine on a fixed input and
a natural number $j$, define its acceptance probability after using $j$ random bits as
the probability that running the machine from $C$ with those random bits yields an
accepting configuration.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance under configuration equivalence]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accepting_congr}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accepting_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and
let $C$ and $D$ be configurations on that input. If their states, input-head positions,
work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions agree, and their output lists have the
same summary (empty, exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to become
$[\mathrm{true}]$ by appending symbols), then $C$ is halted with output exactly
$[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if $D$ is.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability invariance]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_congr}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP, Randomized.PolyAmp.accepting_congr, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and
let $C$ and $D$ be configurations on that input. If their states, input-head positions,
work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions agree, and their output lists have the
same summary (empty, exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to become
$[\mathrm{true}]$ by appending symbols), then for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ the probability
that a uniformly random length-$j$ choice word leads from $C$ to a halted configuration
with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ equals the corresponding probability from $D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability at zero steps]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_zero}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.PolyAmp.accP, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_const, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and
let $C$ be a configuration on that input. The probability that a uniformly random choice
word of length zero leads from $C$ to a halted configuration with output exactly
$[\mathrm{true}]$ is $1$ if $C$ is already halted with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$,
and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step acceptance probability recurrence]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_succ}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP, Randomized.randProb_succ, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and
let $C$ be a configuration on that input. For every $j\in\mathbb{N}$, the probability
that a uniformly random choice word of length $j+1$ leads from $C$ to a halted
configuration with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ is the average of the corresponding
length-$j$ probabilities starting from the configurations reached from $C$ by one step
with choice bit $\mathrm{true}$ and with choice bit $\mathrm{false}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability at initialization]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_init}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.accP_init}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.PolyAmp.accP, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input,
and let $T\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that every choice word of length exactly $T$ leads
from the initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ to a halted configuration. Then the
probability that a uniformly random length-$T$ choice word leads to a halted
configuration whose output is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ equals the probability that the
output after $T$ steps is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting within the configuration code bound]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.haltsWithin_codeBound}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.haltsWithin_codeBound}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPLInP.haltsWithin_of_codes, Randomized.PolyAmp.codeBound, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, $x$ a Boolean input word, and $sp$
a space-bound function. If $N$ uses at most $sp(|y|)$ space on every choice word for
every Boolean input $y$, if $sp(|x|)\le S$, and if $N$ halts on $x$ within $T$ steps
along every branch, then it halts on $x$ within $2^{K(N)(S+\log_2(|x|)+1)}$ steps along
every branch. Here $K(N)$ is twice the encoded chunk width for $N$ plus two, and
$\log_2(n)$ denotes $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Reachable configuration]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
A configuration $C$ of a finite nondeterministic Turing machine on a fixed input is
reachable if some finite sequence of choice bits, when the machine is run from its
initial configuration on that input, produces a configuration with the same core sum as
$C$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Initial configuration is reachable]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.reach_init}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.reach_init}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ on a Boolean input $x$, the
initial configuration of $N$ on $x$ is reachable from itself in the sense that some
choice word produces a configuration with the same machine state, input-head position,
work tapes, work-tape head positions, and output summary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability after one step]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.step}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.step}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let
$x$ be a Boolean input. If a configuration $C$ has the same machine state, input-head
position, work-tape contents and head positions, and output summary as the configuration
reached from the initial configuration on $x$ by some finite word of choice bits, then
for either choice bit $b$, the configuration obtained by taking one step from $C$ under
$b$ also has those same components as a configuration reached from the initial
configuration by a finite word of choice bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachable configurations admit bounded-window representatives]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.inWin}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.inWin}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr, Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.coreSum}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, let $S$ be a natural number, and let $sp$ be a space-bound function.
Suppose every run of $N$ on any input $y$ using any finite choice word visits at most
$sp(|y|)$ distinct work-tape cells in total, and $sp(|x|)\le S$. For every configuration
$C$ reachable on input $x$ in the sense that its state, input-head position, work tapes,
work-head positions, and output summary agree with those of some run, there is a
configuration $D$ whose work heads lie within distance $S$ of the origin and whose work
tapes are blank outside that window, with the same state, input-head position, work
tapes, work-head positions, and output summary as $C$, and with the same configuration
code at window size $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial-configuration language characterization]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_initLang_iff}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_initLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S,c$ be natural numbers. The encoding of $x$, $c$,
and $S$ belongs to the initial-configuration language of $N$ if and only if $c$ equals
the code, at space bound $S$, of the initial configuration of $N$ on input $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance-language characterization]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_acceptLang_iff}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_acceptLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Randomized.PolyAmp.Accepting, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach.inWin, Randomized.PolyAmp.accepting_congr, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S$ be a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most
$sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$, and $sp(\lvert x\rvert)\le S$. If a
configuration $C$ on input $x$ is reachable from the initial configuration by some
sequence of choice bits, then the encoding of $x$, the configuration code of $C$ at
space bound $S$, and $S$ belongs to the acceptance language of $N$ if and only if $C$ is
halted and its output is exactly the one-bit word $[1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Step-language characterization]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_stepLang_iff}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.mem_stepLang_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Randomized.BPLInP.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq, Randomized.BPLInP.inWin_run, Randomized.PolyAmp.Reach, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinNDTM.UsesSpace, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet,
let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S$ be a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most
$sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$, and $sp(\lvert x\rvert)\le S$. If $C$ is a
reachable configuration on input $x$, then, for every natural number $c'$, the encoding
of $x$, the code of $C$ at space bound $S$, the number $c'$, and $S$ belongs to the step
language of $N$ if and only if there is a choice bit $b\in\{0,1\}$ such that $c'$ is the
code at space bound $S$ of the configuration obtained by taking choice $b$ from $C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Configuration code bound]
\lean{Randomized.PolyAmp.cfgCode_lt_codeBound}
\label{Randomized.PolyAmp.cfgCode_lt_codeBound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt, Randomized.PolyAmp.codeBound, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, Boolean input word $x$, natural
number $S$, and configuration $C$ of $N$ on $x$, the code of $C$ using window size $S$
is less than $2^{K(N)(S+\log_2(|x|)+1)}$, where $K(N)$ is twice the encoded chunk width
for $N$ plus two, and $\log_2(n)$ here denotes the specified quantity $\lfloor\log_2
n\rfloor+1$.
\end{theorem}
